goal: A React Native Reusables port of Vercel's AI Elements — universal iOS, Android and Web AI chat and agent UI, distributed as a copy-paste registry.
vibe: Match React Native Reusables for all shared vocabulary — radius, spacing rhythm, type ramp, borders, press states, motion durations — while genuinely new AI surfaces (streaming shimmer, tool status badges, reasoning trace) carry their own visual treatment so an agent action reads as distinct from ordinary app chrome. Distinctness comes from composition and existing roles only; the library declares no new tokens.

notes.dual_engine: The registry emits BOTH nativewind and uniwind variants at 32/32 parity, mirroring RNR. Measured basis: RNR's own two variants differ only by an import-path segment and formatting — 125 identical class tokens, zero nativewind-only classes, and the only two uniwind-only classes live in icon.tsx, which we consume from RNR rather than write. Our source stays engine-agnostic; the build fans it out by rewriting the alias segment and the registryDependencies URL segment.
notes.harness_engine: Storybook runs on ONE engine (uniwind) because a sandbox needs a single bundler. The nativewind variant is validated by CI installing it into a clean Expo app and typechecking, which is proportionate given the emitted delta is an import path.
notes.customization: Consumers get RNR's own customization contract unchanged: the library declares no tokens (verified — RNR registry items ship no cssVars and no theme.ts), and components ride cn + cva + TextClassContext through the consumer's aliases. A consumer on either RNR setup is supported.
notes.prd_correction_needed: PRD 01-scope.md and 11-technical-requirements/ record 'Uniwind-only for v1' with a named deferral trigger. That trigger has fired. AGENTS.md Tech Stack says the same. Both need updating to dual-engine.
notes.scaffold_gate: Deliberately still PENDING. The workflow's step 9 requires the sandbox to run and token stories to render; Storybook is not installed yet. Marking the gate passed before Storybook exists would be fake success.
notes.pin_corrections: Three corrections verified against sources, not inferred: react-native is 0.86.3 (Expo 57's pin, confirmed by Expo's own scaffolder) not 0.87.1; @react-native-reusables/cli is 1.0.0 not 0.7.1; Expo 57's template pins typescript ~6.0.3 while AGENTS.md/PRD say 7.0.2 — harness runs 6.0.3, workspace root holds 7.0.2.
notes.cli_findings: RNR's `init` is interactive and cannot be scripted (hangs on a TTY prompt with piped stdin). `add` works non-interactively with --yes --all --overwrite --styling-library. components.json REQUIRES aliases.utils — omitting it fails validation with 'Invalid components.json'. RNR's doctor asks for tailwindcss-animate even on the uniwind path, which is a Tailwind v3 plugin the styling contract forbids in the uniwind emit.
notes.hoisting_correction: node-linker=hoisted was REMOVED. It was added on the assumption that pnpm's symlinks trip Metro; that assumption was wrong for Expo 57 / Metro, and hoisting actively broke dual-engine support by flattening nativewind into the root where it resolved tailwindcss@4 instead of its package-local v3. With pnpm's default isolated linker, apps/harness resolves tailwindcss 4.3.3 and apps/harness-nativewind resolves 3.4.19, and both engines build.
notes.engine_toggle: The Storybook Engine toolbar item cannot hot-swap engines — both are bundler transforms and NativeWind 4 requires Tailwind v3 while Uniwind requires v4. It reports the running engine and hard-refreshes to the other server, which is why each engine has its own workspace package and port.
notes.rtk_warning: `rtk` wraps tsc and reported 'TypeScript: No errors found' on a run that exited 1 with a real TS2688 error. Verify gates with the direct binary when an exit code and the printed output disagree.
notes.sandbox_scope: The sandbox contains ONLY components this library ships. RNR already exports tokens and Button, and consumers get those from RNR directly, so re-storying them here would duplicate RNR and demo nothing installable. The scaffold smoke stories (RNR Button, design tokens) were deleted once they had done their job of proving the pipeline; their evidence is recorded above.
